name: Policy and Regulation
summary: Uganda's policy, regulatory, and institutional framework for agri-energy — from national energy policy to sector-specific regulations, standards, and incentive mechanisms.
description: Effective agri-energy deployment depends significantly on an enabling policy and regulatory environment. This thematic area examines Uganda's national and sector-level policies relevant to agri-energy, including the National Energy Policy, the Renewable Energy Feed-in Tariff (REFiT) framework, agricultural machinery standards, import duty concessions for energy equipment, and coordination between the energy, agriculture, and water sectors. It also covers the institutional landscape — ERA, UEDCL, MAAIF, NREP — and how their mandates relate to agri-energy. Policy briefs and evidence documents are curated in this section to support sector practitioners engaging with policy processes.
whyItMatters: Policy and regulatory barriers — including high import duties on solar equipment, lack of quality standards, unclear roles between energy and agriculture ministries, and poor access to formal credit for agri-energy — are among the factors limiting scale. Addressing these barriers requires evidence-based advocacy and policy engagement that this platform seeks to support.
